analyzed_vuln.description: ValidateArray calls array.null_count() (line 269) before validating buffer sizes/consistency. For malformed IPC-produced ArrayData, null_count() triggers ArrayData::GetNullCount(), which calls CountSetBits on buffers[0] using offset/length without checking that the null bitmap buffer is large enough. This allows an out-of-bounds bitmap read in CountSetBits (crash at bit_util.cc:95). Root cause is validation order / missing precondition checks in ValidateArray (and transitively GetNullCount usage).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: FuzzIpcStream reads attacker-controlled IPC stream into RecordBatches, then calls RecordBatch::ValidateFull(). A crafted array must have inconsistent metadata such that null bitmap buffer is present but too small (or offset/length too large for it), while null_count is unknown so GetNullCount recomputes it. During ValidateArray, the early null_count() call executes CountSetBits over invalid bitmap range, causing wild read/SEGV.
